papers.title_as_printed: Novel density profile for isothermal cores of dark matter halos
papers.authors_short: Tran, Shen, Vogelsberger, Gilman, O'Neil, Roche, Zier, Gao
papers.identity_note: Title and author list match expected record exactly. arXiv:2411.11945v4, dated March 13 2026, published Phys. Rev. D 113(6), March 2026.
papers.profile_or_method_summary: Proposes a novel analytic density profile (ρ_T25, Eq. 11) for SIDM halos with isothermal cores: ρ_T25(r) = ρ_c [tanh(r/r_c)/(r/r_c)]^n [1 + (r/r_s)^γ]^((3−n)/γ) with γ=2 fixed. Free parameters: ρ_c (core density), r_c (core radius), r_s (scale radius), n (transition index). Core velocity dispersion given by Eq. 12. Validated against idealized N-body simulations of a 10^8 M⊙ halo with σ/m = 21.94 cm^2/g (and 31.98 cm^2/g in smaller dataset). The profile accurately captures both density and velocity dispersion across evolutionary stages from early thermalization to deep core collapse. Transition index n evolves from 1 (NFW) to ~2.5 and remains stable. Fitting errors are negligible vs. direct measurement uncertainties. Outperforms Read, Robertson-Fischer, and Yang profiles in velocity dispersion reconstruction.

caveats: Display math in extracted text is corrupted (e.g., Eq. 11 shows as fragmented symbols); functional form reported as words + raw fragment for human verification.
Simulation limited to velocity-independent cross-section (VICS) models; velocity-dependent cross-sections not tested.
Profile shows slight deviations from simulated velocity dispersion around r_s; a more complex form with additional DOF would be needed for better reconstruction.
Fitting uses log-space least-squares prioritizing core over outer regions (not statistically exact).

papers.title_as_printed: The AIDA-TNG project: dark matter profiles and concentrations in alternative dark matter models
papers.authors_short: Despali, Giocoli, Moscardini, Pillepich, Vogelsberger, Meneghetti et al.
papers.identity_note: Title and author list match expected record. arXiv:2512.15869v2, accepted A&A, published 2026-03-26, DOI 10.1051/0004-6361/202558686.
papers.profile_or_method_summary: AIDA-TNG cosmological simulations (two boxes: 110.7 and 51.7 Mpc) with DMO and full-physics runs across CDM, WDM (1,3 keV), SIDM1 (constant σ/m=1 cm^2/g), and vSIDM (velocity-dependent, Correa 2021 model). Halo mass range 10^9.5–10^14.5 M⊙. Profiles fit with NFW, Einasto, and Y24 (Yang et al. 2024, β=4) models. Resolution limits: r≥4.4 kpc (100/A), r≥1.7 kpc (50/A). In DMO, SIDM forms large flat cores best fit by Y24; core size increases with mass in SIDM1 but reverses in vSIDM (larger cores at low mass). Core radius r_c < scale radius r_Y, so concentrations match CDM when using Y24. In FP runs, baryons suppress SIDM cores via adiabatic contraction (central density enhancement factor ~30 for SIDM vs ~4 for CDM at high mass), and Einasto becomes preferred fit. SIDM1 halos at M_200c~10^12–13 M⊙ show steep cusps γ<−1.5 (gravothermal contraction precursor). Core size–mass relations: y(SIDM1)=0.37−0.5x+0.0026x^2, y(vSIDM)=0.16−0.11x (x=log M_200c, y=log(r_c/r_200c)).

SIDM cross-sections simulated (1 cm^2/g constant, vSIDM peaking at ~1 cm^2/g) are far below the project's fiducial 483 cm^2/g at 29.4 km/s.
vSIDM model is specifically the Correa (2021) implementation; not a general velocity-dependent model.
FP runs show resolution-dependent behavior for M_200c=[10^12,10^13] M⊙ where stellar component dominates.
AIDA-TNG halos do not form density cores from baryonic feedback (unlike some other hydro simulations).

papers.title_as_printed: Dark matter density profiles of the Milky Way satellite population: reconciling simulations and observations
papers.identity_note: Title and author list match expected record. arXiv:2607.08818v2, accepted A&A, 20 pages, 11 figures (manuscript shows 14 pages + appendices).
papers.profile_or_method_summary: Compares NIHAO and FIRE-2 cosmological zoom-in simulations (CDM + baryons) against dynamical models of 16 MW dwarf satellites from four methods (R19, H20/H23, AP25, P25/P26). Key innovation: measures inner slopes at fixed physical radii (100, 250, 500 pc) instead of fixed fraction of R_vir, enabling apples-to-apples comparison. Stellar mass range M_⋆ ~ 10^3–10^8 M⊙ (observed), simulations up to 10^11 M⊙. Fits double power-law (Zhao 1996) to simulated profiles. Defines reliability radii from spectroscopic catalogs (50 stars inner, 10 stars outer for star-by-star; 3 bins for binned). NFW baseline from Moster et al. (2013) + Moliné et al. (2023) via abundance matching. Main result: clear mass-dependent core formation trend; simulations agree with observations within ≲1σ for most systems in density space, outperforming NFW. No SIDM cross-section constraints.

caveats: No SIDM cross-section constraints or sigma/m values — this is a CDM+baryons paper.
Display math in extracted text is corrupted; slope values from Tables A.1–A.3 are reliable as they appear as plain numbers.
Ultra-faint dwarfs (M_⋆ < 10^5 M⊙) have very limited observational data (40–65 stars) and no close simulated mass matches.
R19 dataset has tighter uncertainties, making it harder to match; some tensions reflect dataset-to-dataset differences.
Antlia 2 and Crater 2 are likely extreme tidal outliers; Willman 1 has compactness and binary-star issues.
Convergence radii: FIRE-2 uses r_200p (200 DM particles), NIHAO uses Power et al. (2003) with Schaller et al. (2015) threshold f(r)≥0.33.
